subject.title: fix(sqlite): allow verified shared wal backports

question: Should OpenClaw permit an operator-asserted environment override for a shared SQLite build whose safety backport cannot be detected from `sqlite_version()`?
rationale: The implementation intentionally trades a strict corruption guard for an unverifiable operator assertion; code review cannot decide whether that is the repository’s acceptable data-integrity boundary.

options.title: Require an explicit documented exception path
options.body: Keep the override only with a canonical verification recipe and real affected-image proof showing the default rejection and verified successful startup.

options.title: Keep the current version guard absolute
options.body: Reject all versions outside the known-safe upstream maintenance lines until the runtime can prove the vendor backport.

options.title: Accept the bare override
options.body: Treat `OPENCLAW_ASSUME_SYSTEM_SQLITE_WAL_RESET_SAFE=1` as sufficient operator responsibility without additional documentation or runtime proof.

recommendation.title: Require an explicit documented exception path
recommendation.body: Keep the override only with a canonical verification recipe and real affected-image proof showing the default rejection and verified successful startup.
